CodeQL rule that flags suspicious comparisons between index-based and max-sized expressions.

# Purpose
This CodeQL query detects suspicious relational comparisons between index-based expressions and max-sized expressions in C and C++ code. It defines name-based expression classes for index terms such as `idx`, `index`, or single-letter loop variables, and for size terms such as `max`, `size`, and `length`. The `wrongComparison` predicate matches comparison operators that can cause off-by-one errors when an index is compared against an upper bound, such as `<=`, `>`, `>=`, or `<` in the wrong direction. When the query finds a match, it reports a warning that the comparison may be wrong if the index is expected to stay in the range `[0, max)`.
